cells.tense: The sense of what is fair is running on feeling that has been lived all the way through.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Forgive a debt someone has carried long enough that only a scorekeeper would still be counting it. Waive it outright, no conditions, and don't bring it up between you again.
cells.core:
Between people, what has gone out of proportion can be felt and still weighed level, because the feeling has finished rather than been cut short. Nothing gets ruled on before it has been lived through, and nothing after, either — the ruling and the feeling arrive as one thing. That is what right proportion looks like from inside a body: not a verdict handed down once the evidence is in, just the settled weight of a matter fully gone through.

This week, forgive a debt — the thing someone has owed you so long that only someone keeping score would still be counting it. Name it, release it, and keep your books between you shut on it. You were already leaning toward the feeling that had done its time. The balance doesn't need the repayment to be right; the scale just needs to be honest about what's still owed. What it costs is the account you kept to prove the wrong happened. The wrong doesn't need the page.
cells.sheetLine: The scale stays level without anyone's debts on it.
cells.verb: seeing a way through without seeing the end — taking the next step on the light there is.
cells.place: where what has gone out of proportion between people gets weighed and set level.

cells.tense: The sense of what is fair will not be ready to use until the whole picture has been carried around.
cells.act: protect the young thing from being judged early
cells.ask: Hold one thing that's still forming out from under a verdict this week — no report back, no comparison, no saying how it's going. Let it stay unnamed a while.
cells.core:
Where things between people are weighed, the picture gets finished before anything is decided. Every matter arrives complete in the mind — whole road, both meanings, all of it — and gets judged there, where it is finished, instead of out here, where it isn't. The next step goes missing under a reading that belongs further on. The weighing keeps its exactness and stops being any help.

Protect one young thing from being read too early. A plan, a change in how you live that hasn't happened yet, a piece of work still wet — keep it out from under the verdict for a season. Not everything needs a name this week; some things need only to stay unnamed and still growing. That is care that doesn't exhaust itself: if you can already tell how it's going, it's already being judged. What it costs is the confidence of a named shape.
cells.sheetLine: You finish the picture before the step gets to happen.
cells.verb: seeing a way through without seeing the end — taking the next step on the light there is.
cells.place: where what has gone out of proportion between people gets weighed and set level.

cells.tense: The sense of what is fair has been resting on conclusions drawn before the feeling was let in.
cells.act: notice what you already know before you reason about it
cells.ask: For one dispute still open between you and someone, name what you knew at first sight, before the reasons, and read that line before you decide anything.
cells.core:
Where things between people get set level, the picture has been finished in the mind and then trusted as if a finished picture were a use. Trust in the deeper floor is gone: only the drawing is allowed, and nothing that arrives before the evidence is permitted inside. The step goes unseen, and the scale tips toward the proof page, which is thin.

Let the first sight stand. Before you weigh a matter this week, name what you knew at first glance, before the reasons, and read it before you decide anything at all. It will be short and it will not argue well — let it win the first round on those grounds. It is the seed of fair judgment, not the judgment itself, and you're only being asked to plant it. What you turn to next grows out of it.
cells.sheetLine: You weigh it after the first sight has already been thrown out.
cells.verb: seeing a way through without seeing the end — taking the next step on the light there is.
cells.place: where what has gone out of proportion between people gets weighed and set level.

cells.tense: The sense of what is fair is being kept by a plan nobody has noticed is a plan.
cells.act: keep the steady light lit by attention, not flash
cells.ask: Fifteen minutes alone, same plain thing each day for a week — the small version of something you make or keep. No redesign, no plan, just the doing of it again.
cells.core:
Between people, the balance is being held — by someone who doesn't count themselves among the ones holding it. Reading the room, shifting a weight, saying afterward that it just turned out that way. The ledgers have a writer and the writer has no name for the writing. The knowledge of what's being kept level is real, and it's filed under not mine.

Do the plain version again, alone, for fifteen minutes. Something you make or keep — not improved, not finished, just done again with attention. The small light is kept lit by attention rather than by flash. Repeated practice is the plain form of knowing what to tend, and it will start telling you what you're keeping level before you've decided to look. It starts before any final account.
cells.sheetLine: What's kept level between people is being kept by you, unnamed.
